T0.scene_summary: A pink conference room with a long table, wheeled chairs, framed wall panels, and a checkerboard floor.

main_defects.evidence: A dark, framed door occupies a substantial vertical strip on the right in the reference, while no corresponding door appears in the reconstruction.

The reference wall panels also have a reflective or translucent appearance that is largely absent in the reconstruction.

main_defects.evidence: The near-side reference chair backs are rounded and taper into curved seats, while the corresponding reconstruction backs are straight-edged rectangles.
main_defects.uncertainty: Some differences in visible seat shape are affected by occlusion and camera angle.

main_defects.description: The left framed panel group is more cropped and occupies a smaller portion of the wall in the reconstruction; the back panel also appears broader and shorter relative to the visible wall.
main_defects.evidence: The complete left group is visible in the reference, but its left end is cut off in the reconstruction, and the back panel's apparent aspect ratio differs.
main_defects.uncertainty: Cropping and perspective can explain part of the apparent difference in proportions.

strengths: The overall conference-room arrangement with a long rectangular table and chairs on both sides is recognizable.
Pink walls, a checkered floor, white baseboards, and framed rectangular wall features are present.
The chairs have pale upholstery and dark wheeled bases, and the table has dark supporting legs.
A small green plant is suggested near the far end of the table.
T0.uncertainty: This is a coarse automated visual judgment of two single images, not a human rating or a validated aggregate metric. Differences in camera position, framing, illumination and occlusion may account for some apparent omissions and proportions; hidden geometry cannot be assessed.

T1.scene_summary: A pink conference room with a long meeting table, wheeled chairs, framed wall openings and a checkerboard floor.
T1.overall_evidence: The reconstruction captures the room type, main furniture arrangement, wall color and checkerboard pattern. Its viewpoint and framing differ substantially, the prominent dark foreground door is absent, the chairs have noticeably different silhouettes, and the glossy, dark material treatment of the reference is largely missing.

main_defects.description: The large dark teal paneled door that occupies the right foreground of the reference is not visible in the reconstruction.
main_defects.evidence: The reference has a prominent dark vertical door with recessed panels and a horizontal bar; the reconstruction shows the table and room wall at the right edge instead.
main_defects.uncertainty: The door could be outside the reconstruction camera's field of view rather than absent from the scene.

main_defects.description: The reconstruction is framed closer to the table and at a different angle, with much less open foreground floor and a visible gray ceiling band.
main_defects.evidence: In the reference the table sits in the rear half beyond a broad area of floor, while in the reconstruction it spans nearly the full width and foreground chairs are cropped at the bottom.
main_defects.uncertainty: Differences in room or furniture proportions may contribute alongside camera placement and field of view.

main_defects.description: The reconstruction is much lighter and more matte: the floor lacks the dark glossy reflections and the tabletop lacks the reference's strong streaked, mirror-like surface. The wall openings also read as opaque white panels rather than softly reflective or translucent glass.
main_defects.evidence: The reference floor has dark brown and charcoal tiles with prominent bright reflections, and its table has irregular light reflections; the reconstruction uses pale pink-gray checks and a relatively uniform pale table.
main_defects.uncertainty: Lighting and viewpoint can also affect apparent color and reflectivity; the exact material of the reference openings is uncertain.

main_defects.description: The reconstructed chair backs are tall, flat rectangular slabs, unlike the reference's rounded, tapered upholstered backs and more curved seats.
main_defects.evidence: Multiple foreground chairs in the reference have rounded shoulder and lower edges, whereas those in the reconstruction have broad, nearly rectangular vertical backs.
main_defects.uncertainty: Perspective and partial occlusion affect individual chair outlines.

main_defects.description: The long left-wall opening is cropped by the left image edge in the reconstruction, while the reference shows its complete framed outline; the back-wall opening also appears higher relative to the table.
main_defects.evidence: The reference's left frame begins visibly inside the image and the far opening sits close above the chairs. The reconstruction cuts off the left frame and leaves a larger gap below the far panel.
main_defects.uncertainty: These screen-space differences may be primarily caused by camera framing rather than actual placement.

strengths: The long rectangular conference table and rows of wheeled office chairs convey the same meeting-room arrangement.
Pink walls, white baseboards, a multi-section left wall opening, and a separate rectangular far-wall opening are present.
The floor retains a small-scale checkerboard pattern, and a small plant is suggested near the back of the table.
T1.uncertainty: This is a coarse automated estimate based only on the two supplied images, not a human rating or validated aggregate metric. Different camera framing and illumination may explain some apparent layout, proportion and material differences; occluded or off-frame geometry cannot be assessed.
